content.text: The verifier's feedback this round affirms every substantive element: status, cited text, party mapping, the absence of a redline, byte-identical paragraphs, and the out-of-scope exclusivity note. The sole failing check — general-solicitation carve-out — is expressly characterized as non-probative and consistent with absence rather than a defect. There is no substantive defect left to repair, and manufacturing a carve-out to satisfy the check would require drafting the very restriction the rule tells us to avoid. I'll resubmit the finding unchanged in substance.

input.quote: 10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
input.rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

Party mapping: our client, The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("the Company"), is the customer under this site development and hosting agreement; HDI is the vendor/host. The rule's concern is a covenant binding Customer, and none exists.

On the outstanding "general-solicitation carve-out" check: this is not a defect and cannot be cured. The check tests an attribute that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause, as does the companion 12-month duration check. With no such clause in the document, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to attach. Drafting a carve-out would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, importing a personnel restriction on us that the counterparty never sought and moving us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.
